scenario: We launch this invoicing service next week. Do a security audit of it first.
fixture: evaluations/fixtures/security-auditor (small multi-tenant Flask invoicing API with planted vulnerabilities and one safe decoy query)
required_behaviors: finds the SQL injection in invoice search, tracing the query parameter to the f-string query
finds the IDOR on GET /invoices/<id>: login is checked but invoice ownership (account_id) is not
finds the path traversal in /download where the file parameter is joined onto the exports directory without containment
flags MD5 password hashing and the hardcoded SECRET_KEY / DB password / DEBUG config
ranks findings by reachability and impact with a one-line justification and gives a specific fix for each
forbidden_behaviors: reporting the parameterized invoice_report query in db.py as SQL injection
modifying the application code without being asked
grading_notes: Pass if all required_behaviors are observed in SECURITY_AUDIT.md and the decoy (db.invoice_report) is either ruled out or not reported. Finding the unsafe yaml.load import is expected by the answer key but not gated. Compare against evaluations/answers/security-auditor.md.
